s272-D1.label: How many primary buttons per what — and what is the 'what'?
s272-D1.chosen_option: One primary per LAYOUT REGION as defined by our app-shell (page header · main · action bar · each modal surface) — our own vocabulary rather than an imported one.

quotes.IBM Carbon: Primary buttons should only appear once per screen
quotes.Atlassian: Only include one primary button or call to action (CTA) in a page
quotes.Fluent 2: Only use one primary button in a layout for the most important action.
quotes.Ant Design: there can be at most one primary button in a section.
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Don't use more than one primary button in a section or screen
quotes.Adobe Spectrum: Don't use more than 3 accent buttons in the same view.
quotes.USWDS: Avoid using too many buttons on a page.
quotes.NN/g: Primary buttons have the most visual emphasis to grab user attention
quotes.OURS: button.meta antiPatterns[0]: 'Using more than one primary button in a single context' — 'context' is undefined

s272-D1.why_contested: The COUNT is near-unanimous (1) with one outlier (3). The SCOPE word is not: screen · page · layout · section · view. No gate can check 'context'.
options: One primary per SCREEN (Carbon's word) — strictest, catches a primary in a card inside a page that already has one.
One primary per SECTION (Ant/Polaris) — allows a page-level primary plus one per card or panel.
One primary per LAYOUT REGION as defined by our app-shell (page header · main · action bar · each modal surface) — our own vocabulary rather than an imported one.
Leave 'context' undefined and keep the rule advisory.
s272-D1.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3. It is the only wording that names things our library already has, so a gate can walk the DOM and count. Carbon's 'screen' is the closest external match and explicitly excludes the app header, modal and side panel — which is option 3 in different words.

s272-D2.label: tags-input
s272-D2.when_gate: the committed values are the USER'S OWN words AND no option list can be offered AND each value becomes a removable Tags chip AND a half-typed value is committed on blur, never discarded
s272-D2.when_prose: beats combobox (#270: "options >= 16, closed list") and multi-select (#270: "the answer is a set") on the single test our meta already states — is there a list at all; where a list exists the answer belongs to one of those two, and where it does not, only this component is honest (it explicitly does not claim role=combobox without a list, our antiPatterns[3]); the chip itself is the gated Tags atom, so any chip change lands in Tags first.

s272-D3.label: At what list length does a record-list get pagination?

quotes.Polaris: Paginate when the current list contains more than 50 items.
quotes.IBM Carbon: When there is too much data to display on one page
quotes.Ant Design: When it will take a long time to load/render all items.
quotes.USWDS: silent — the page carries no when-to-use section at all
quotes.NN/g: silent on a number; argues against infinite scroll instead

options: Carry no number: gate on "more than one screen of rows" (device-relative, testable in a fixture).
Carry no number and no gate — pagination stays a composer's judgement, prose only.
s272-D3.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. 50 is one system's number with no research cited, and a 40-row table on a phone already needs pagination. This is the exact shape of s270-D1 — if Dave rules a number here he should rule it the same way (provisional, with a tripwire).
